shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower on Wednesday for a second straight day, after rising early in the previous session to the highest level in nearly three years.

children: Chicago Board of Trade corn futures closed lower on Wednesday for a second straight day, after rising early in the previous session to the highest level in nearly three years.
Traders were waiting to see whether China would agree to buy US farm goods in conjunction with a highly anticipated summit between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping on Thursday.
"Pre-negotiations with the Chinese have elicited no indication of any grain deal to be announced," Marex said in a note.
Traders monitored rain delaying US harvests.
Rain showers were returning across western corn and soybean production areas, including parts of Nebraska and South Dakota, the US Department of Agriculture said in a daily weather forecast.
CBOT December corn (CZ26) ended down 7-3/4 cents at $5.29 per bushel.
